Enabling Loop Recording resolved it — new events are now saving, so the standard L1 fix succeeded.

repair_steps: Confirm with customer that new events are saving and no error E-402 is displayed.
Advise customer to export any important clips before they are overwritten by loop recording.

Close the case as resolved by standard L1 fix.
output.customer_reply: We've resolved the issue by enabling Loop Recording on your base station. New events are now saving normally. Please note that loop recording will automatically overwrite the oldest clips when storage is full, so export any important footage you wish to keep. If you need further assistance, feel free to reach out.

args.query: E-402 storage full loop recording fix procedure

args.action: In the app, go to Base Station Settings > Storage and enable Loop Recording. This will automatically overwrite the oldest clips so the storage never fills up again. (If the customer wants to keep existing clips, first export them, then either enable loop recording or format the storage.)

results.text: Base station storage at or above 98 percent with loop recording disabled. Frontline action: enable loop recording or format storage.

Event clips are stored on the base station's internal eMMC (HB-100: 16 GB, HB-200: 32 GB). When loop recording is disabled and storage reaches 98 percent, new events are not recorded and error E-402 is shown. Enable loop recording in Base Station Settings > Storage, or format the storage after exporting clips.

Solid blue: online and connected to cloud. Blinking blue: pairing mode (lasts 120 seconds). Solid red: no internet uplink. Blinking red: booting or firmware update in progress, do not unplug. Solid purple: storage almost full (over 95 percent).
